![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14108214/assets/e2591e9da960008980cf96184975ef19713735814183a97ca8c8f784536fced5.png)

Describe the shaded region shown above using set-builder notation.

$$
{(x,y)\in {{field-1}}\,:\,-x-3\,{{field-2}}\,y\,{{field-3}}\,x+4}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
The points in our set include all those that lie *above* the line $y=-x-3$ and *below* the line $y=x+4.$

A point $P(x,y)$ lies *inside* the shaded region if the following conditions are satisfied:

$$
y>-x-3,\,y<x+4.
$$

 

Combining this into a single condition, we have

$$
-x-3<y<x+4.
$$

We must also include the lines $y=-x-3$ and $y=x+4$ since the boundaries are included in the set (the lines are solid). So, we change the corresponding inequality symbols above as follows:

$$
-x-3\le y\le x+4
$$

Moreover, since we're considering *every* real value in this region, $x\in R,y\in R,$ and therefore 

$$
(x,y)\in R\times R={R}^{2}.
$$

Therefore, we can write the set as

$$
{(x,y)\in {R}^{2}\,:\,-x-3\le y\le x+4}.
$$

questions.worked_solution:
The points in our set include all those that lie *below* the line $y=4$ and *below* the line $y=4x+1.$

A point $P(x,y)$ lies *inside* the shaded region if the following conditions are satisfied:

$$
y<4,\,y<4x+1.
$$

We must also include the lines $y=4$ and $y=4x+1$ since the boundaries are included in the set (the lines are solid). So, we change the corresponding inequality symbols above as follows:

$$
y\le 4,\,y\le 4x+1
$$

Moreover, since we're considering *every* real value in this region, $x\in R,y\in R,$ and therefore 

$$
(x,y)\in R\times R={R}^{2}.
$$

Therefore, we can write the set as

$$
{(x,y)\in {R}^{2}\,:\,y\le 4,\,y\le 4x+1}.
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Describing Non-Rectangular Sets Using Set-Builder Notation
questions.worked_solution:
The equation of an ellipse centered at the origin with a horizontal radius of length $a$ and a vertical radius of length $b$ is given by

$$
\frac{{x}^{2}}{{a}^{2}}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{{b}^{2}}=1.
$$

 

Here, the elliptical boundary of our region has horizontal radius $a=2$ and vertical radius $b=4.$ Therefore, the equation of the ellipse is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{x}^{2}}{4}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{16} & =1,\end{aligned}
$$

which we can write as

$$
16{x}^{2}+4{y}^{2}=64.
$$

We're interested in describing all points that lie *outside* the ellipse. So, let's pick any point outside the region, say, $(0,5).$ Substituting its coordinates into the equation of the boundary, we obtain

$$
16(0)^{2}+4(5)^{2}\,>\,64.
$$

As a result, the points $P(x,y)$ in our region are any real numbers that satisfy the condition

$$
16{x}^{2}+4{y}^{2}>64.
$$

We must also include the curve $16{x}^{2}+4{y}^{2}=64$ since the boundary is included in the set (the curve is solid). So, we change the inequality symbol above as follows:

$$
16{x}^{2}+4{y}^{2}\ge 64.
$$

Therefore, we can write the set as

$$
{(x,y)\in {R}^{2}\,:\,16{x}^{2}+4{y}^{2}\ge 64}.
$$

Use set builder notation to describe the shaded region given in the diagram above:

$$
{(x,y)\in {{field-1}}\,:\,x\,{{field-2}}\,{y}^{2}}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
The points in our set include all those that lie *to the left* of the curve $x={y}^{2}.$

Therefore, a point $P(x,y)$ lies *inside* the shaded region if the following condition is satisfied:

$$
x<{y}^{2}
$$

Since the boundary is not included in the set (the curve is dashed), the inequality is strict.

Moreover, since we're considering *every* real value in this region, $x\in R,y\in R,$ and therefore 

$$
(x,y)\in R\times R={R}^{2}.
$$

Therefore, we can write the set as

$$
{(x,y)\in {R}^{2}\,:\,x<{y}^{2}}.
$$

questions.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14108214/assets/45690fd9ef862b1c8f0a2bb34bba2d305cd3c723ccde09648133b64006ad8f25.png)

Describe the shaded region shown above using set-builder notation.

$$
{(x,y)\in {{field-1}}\,:\,y\,{{field-2}}\,2}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
Since all points $P(x,y)$ in our set lie at integer values of $x$ and $y,$ we have $x\in Z,y\in Z,$ and therefore 

$$
(x,y)\in Z\times Z={Z}^{2}.
$$

The points in our set include all those that lie *below* the line $y=2.$ For those points, the following condition is satisfied:

$$
y<2
$$

Since the boundary is *not* included in the set (the curve is *not* solid),  no further action must be taken, so we have

$$
y<2.
$$

Therefore, we can write the set as follows:

$$
{(x,y)\in {Z}^{2}\,:\,y<2}
$$
